sections.html:
Spartanburg is the county seat of Spartanburg County, in the Upstate region, about 98 miles northwest of Columbia and 80 miles west of Charlotte. The 2020 census counted 38,732 residents inside the city, and the metro area is far larger at 383,327, so a house inside the city limits sits in a much bigger market than the city population suggests.

The Hub City nickname comes from the railroad lines that once radiated from the town. Textile mills shaped the housing here, with around 40 mills established by the early 1900s, and some neighborhoods still show it.

• Downtown and Morgan Square: the original courthouse village and the city's main hub
  • Hampton Heights: the oldest intact downtown neighborhood, a historic district with Queen Anne, Neoclassical and bungalow homes
  • Northside: home to the Hub City Farmers Market at Harvest Park
  • Beaumont: a former mill and its adjacent mill village, a local historic district
  • Glendale: southeast of the city, near the Glendale Mill ruins

If your house is in a designated historic district, exterior changes may need approval, which can affect how a buyer plans renovations. Rain is steady through the year, so gutters, grading, crawlspace moisture and old roofs are the items a buyer's inspector will find. A seller who knows about them should plan to disclose them or price around them.

Spartanburg County School District 7 runs most city public schools, and its students are zoned to Spartanburg High School. District 6 serves the westernmost part of the city and is zoned to Paul M. Dorman High School. Your zone depends on your address, so confirm it with the district.

Inside town, SPARTA runs eight bus routes, the Amtrak Crescent stops at the Magnolia Street station and the 55-mile Daniel Morgan Trail System links trails, sidewalks and protected bike lanes.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and appeals
sections.html:
Spartanburg County says real estate taxes are due January 15 to avoid penalties. State law adds 3 percent after the due date, another 7 percent in early February and another 5 percent in mid-March.

Tax questionSpartanburg County answer
When to pay without penaltyBy January 15
Can the tax bill itself be appealed?No, and it cannot be paid under protest
Can the appraisal be appealed?Yes, in writing to the Assessor's Office
Owner-occupied home rateMay qualify for the 4 percent assessment rate

The county also says its mass appraisal is for tax purposes only and does not limit your asking price.

sections.h2: What happens to taxes when a house sells
sections.html:
• A sale triggers a reappraisal to current market value, and the 15 percent cap on increases applies only to the regular reappraisals.
  • If you sold during the current year and still got the bill, forward it to the buyer or ask your closing attorney.
  • If you sold after January 1, the new owner is updated in the file for the following tax year.

Settle any unpaid balance before or at closing so the buyer receives a clean title.

sections.h2: Fees on a City of Spartanburg tax bill
sections.html:
City properties can see extra charges on the county bill. The county adds an annual landfill service charge to residential property, and the City of Spartanburg's stormwater and residential garbage fees are loaded together into a single line called the City of Spartanburg Fee Total. Questions about that line go to the city at 864-562-4510, not the county.

Ask the closing attorney to check for unpaid fees tied to the parcel. Unpaid landfill service charges become a lien on the property, ranking behind only the lien for property taxes.

South Carolina's disclosure statute asks most sellers to give a written condition statement before the buyer signs. On each topic the seller may state what they know or make no representation, and the parties can agree to an as-is sale. Transfers by an estate fiduciary or under court order are exempt.

People turn to a cash sale here when a house needs more repair than they can fund, when heirs live out of town, when an old mill-era house has problems an inspection will find, or when a tax or fee balance is piling up. In each case the question is the same: what does the house cost to keep, and what would listing cost in time and repairs?

The buyer's funds replace a mortgage lender, so there is no appraisal or loan approval to wait on. A closing attorney still handles title, pays off liens and records the deed. Compare any written offer against the cost and time of listing, and read the settlement statement line by line.

Before your first call, collect your latest tax notice, a mortgage payoff figure and anything the city has sent you about fees. For an inherited house, add the estate papers.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a Spartanburg house?
faqs.a: Spartanburg County says real estate taxes are due January 15 to avoid penalties. Under state law, penalties of 3, 7 and 5 percent are added in stages after that date.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Spartanburg County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Not the bill itself. The county says taxes cannot be appealed, but the appraisal can be appealed in writing to the Assessor's Office, and time limits apply. There is no provision to pay taxes under protest.

faqs.q: Will the county appraisal limit what I can ask for my Spartanburg house?
faqs.a: No. The county states that its mass appraisal is done for property tax purposes only and does not restrict your asking price.

faqs.q: Why does my Spartanburg tax bill include city fees?
faqs.a: The county loads municipal fees onto the tax notice, including City of Spartanburg stormwater and garbage charges combined in one line. The county directs questions on those fees to the city at 864-562-4510.

faqs.q: Do I have to disclose defects when selling a house in Spartanburg?
faqs.a: Most sellers must give a written property condition statement under South Carolina law, unless the transfer is exempt. You can report what you know or say you make no representation, and a knowingly false answer can create liability.
